PreToolUse._comment: mt#2865 dispatch-intent write gate. Deliberately STANDALONE, not GUARD_REGISTRY/dispatcher: dispatch-pretooluse.ts is registered only under the 'Bash|mcp__minsky__session_exec' matcher block above — the session_commit/session_edit_file/session_write_file/session_search_replace/session_pr_create/session_pr_edit tool family this guard gates is NOT among the tool names that already spawn the dispatcher process, so migrating would require widening THAT block's matcher (extra dispatcher spawns for every guard already registered there, for zero benefit — none of them match this tool family). A standalone registration is the cheaper correct choice here, mirroring block-subagent-merge-without-grant.ts's precedent for the sibling D5 merge guard. session_pr_merge is deliberately excluded — already D5-covered by block-subagent-merge-without-grant.ts above. Timeout=30 (PR #2033 R1 NON-BLOCKING #4): matched to parallel-work-guard.ts's timeout (also 30, below) rather than invented — both are standalone PreToolUse guards reacting to session/dispatch-lifecycle tool calls, a closer shape match than ask-permission-bridge.ts's 60 (that guard does live Ask server verification, a heavier network-bound workload this guard never does — it only reads a local JSON file, plus this PR's new exclusive-create lock retry loop, which itself caps at ~1s well inside 30).

mt#3350 success-criteria injection. Surfaces the bound task's `## Success Criteria` verbatim at PR-creation time, so they are confronted at the moment of shipping rather than recalled from having written them (mem#736 R2; the prose tier for this class — /implement-task §7 item 5 — has a measured 14x recurrence across 13 PRs). Matcher is session_pr_create ALONE, deliberately: the two PreToolUse blocks above that mention the tool are multi-tool matchers that also cover session_commit, and injecting the criteria on every commit would be noise that trains the reader to skip them. Not migrated into the dispatcher/GUARD_REGISTRY for the same reason recorded on the dispatch-intent gate above — session_pr_create is not among the tool names that already spawn the dispatcher. Timeout=20: one `minsky tasks spec get` CLI call (budgeted 15s internally) plus process spawn; matched to the sibling stamp-pr-author-link.ts registration on the same tool rather than invented. Fail-open and silent — no task id, no spec, or no criteria section all exit 0 with no output.

PostToolUse._comment: mt#3257 subagent model verification — observer, never blocks. Compares tool_input.model (requested alias) against tool_response.resolvedModel (both measured in the Agent PostToolUse payload, sync AND async-launch modes — mt#3257 probes) and warns via additionalContext on mismatch, so a dropped tier override can't silently produce false provenance again (the mt#3151 pin incident). Degraded payloads log to .minsky/subagent-model-mismatch.jsonl instead of warning. Matcher covers Task, the same tool's older name, to stay aligned with the hook's TARGET_TOOL_NAMES (PR #2388 R1). Timeout 10: the hook spawns one bun process and does at most one local file append — no subprocess, no network, no DB — so 10s is generous headroom over sibling 5s reminders purely for cold-start jitter. Override: MINSKY_SKIP_SUBAGENT_MODEL_CHECK.

mt#2358 main-workspace mutation observer — advisory, never blocks. Reads the MAIN workspace's git status after a Bash call and names tracked files that became modified during it. Outcome-based rather than syntax-based on purpose: the recurrence that reopened mt#2358 used sed -i, cat >> and a python3 heredoc, none of which a destructive-verb list contains. The channel is uncovered because require-session-for-main-workspace-edits.ts matches only Edit/Write/NotebookEdit (FILE_EDITING_TOOLS, line 99) while the harness's auto mode instructs agents to make file changes with sed and heredocs. The reported set is a DIFF against the last observation, so the tree's pre-existing modified files never flag and each file flags at most once. Timeout 10: one git status (measured 0.03-0.04s in this repo) plus two local file touches — no subprocess chain, no network, no DB. NO override var, deliberately: this injects text and records a fire — there is no decision to bypass, and minting a name is what ADR-028 D3 is retiring.

MessageDisplay._comment: mt#2565: linkifies bare mt#NNNN / PR #N refs in assistant output as it is displayed; the stored transcript keeps the bare ref. This event fires per BATCH OF COMPLETED LINES while a message streams, synchronously in the display path — far hotter than any other event here — so it deliberately does NOT go through the guard dispatcher (ADR-028 D7(5): keep per-invocation IO out of a hot path) and the hook itself loads no domain code. Timeout=5 is a ceiling, not a budget: the measured per-invocation cost is process startup plus a small state-file read. If a SECOND MessageDisplay consumer ever appears, add a dispatch-messagedisplay.ts entrypoint with a transform-shaped outcome rather than a second command here.
